name: Hearing Sensitivity
definition: The ability to detect or tell the differences between sounds that vary in pitch and loudness.

benchmark.name: HEAR
benchmark.human_reference: Workers whose jobs rely on hearing sensitivity, such as musicians, audio technicians and sound engineers, with the general adult workforce as the broader frame.

benchmark.name: MARBLE
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on the NSynth Pitch classification task
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce in roles that use hearing sensitivity, such as audio and sound technicians, equipment and machine operators who listen for faults, and musicians. Most of these people are not trained musicians and do not have absolute pitch.

benchmark.name: DeafTest
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on two-choice loudness-comparison and pitch-comparison tasks; 50% = chance

benchmark.name: STAR-Bench
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on multiple-choice questions, Foundational Acoustic Perception average
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing, the typical person who uses pitch and loudness discrimination at work (e.g., noticing alarm tones or machine sounds, basic audio monitoring).

benchmark.name: SonicBench
benchmark.metric: overall accuracy (%) averaged across all 12 attributes and both task types; chance is 50%, human average is 91%
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing, the typical person making everyday pitch and loudness judgments at work. SonicBench's human participants (average 91%) are the proxy.
